title: Indian Contract Act, 1872 — Section 4 (Communication when complete)

content.overview: Section 4 provides that the communication of a proposal is complete when it comes to the knowledge of the person to whom it is made. The communication of an acceptance is complete — as against the proposer, when it is put in a course of transmission to him so as to be out of the power of the acceptor; as against the acceptor, when it comes to the knowledge of the proposer. The communication of a revocation is complete — as against the person who makes it, when it is put into a course of transmission to the person to whom it is made so as to be out of the power of the person who makes it; as against the person to whom it is made, when it comes to his knowledge.
content.glance: Proposal complete on knowledge; acceptance complete on posting vs knowledge; revocation complete on despatch vs knowledge.
content.study: Proposal is complete when it comes to the offeree’s knowledge. Acceptance is complete as against the proposer when put in a course of transmission out of the acceptor’s power, and as against the acceptor when it comes to the proposer’s knowledge. Revocation is complete as against the maker when put in a course of transmission out of the maker’s power, and as against the recipient when it comes to the recipient’s knowledge. Current-law framing: identify proposal/acceptance/revocation; apply the knowledge or course-of-transmission limb; then apply s. 5 for the revocation cut-off.

sections.heading: Proposal
sections.body: Complete when it comes to the knowledge of the person to whom it is made.

sections.heading: Acceptance
sections.body: As against proposer: when put in a course of transmission out of the acceptor’s power. As against acceptor: when it comes to the proposer’s knowledge.

sections.heading: Revocation
sections.body: As against the maker: when put in a course of transmission out of the maker’s power. As against the recipient: when it comes to the recipient’s knowledge.

examples.title: Acceptance by post
examples.body: B accepts A’s proposal by letter. As against A, acceptance is complete when the letter is posted; as against B, when A receives it.

hypotheticals.question: When is a posted acceptance complete against the proposer?
hypotheticals.analysis: When it is put in a course of transmission so as to be out of the power of the acceptor (s. 4).

distinctions.title: When communication is complete (s. 4) vs when revocation is still possible (s. 5)
distinctions.left: Timing rules for proposal, acceptance, revocation
distinctions.right: Cut-off for revoking proposal or acceptance

misconceptions.trap: Acceptance is never complete until the proposer actually reads it.
misconceptions.correction: As against the proposer, acceptance is complete when put in a course of transmission out of the acceptor’s power.

questionsAndAnswers.question: How should a Section 4 problem be analysed?
questionsAndAnswers.answer: I. Identify proposal, acceptance or revocation. II. Apply the knowledge or course-of-transmission limb. III. Link to s. 5 for revocation cut-off. IV. Conclude.

examTips: Memorise the three pairs of completion rules.
Always pair with s. 5 on revocation.
